correctness.rationale: After closed-neighborhood observation, exactly the cells in empty-row×empty-column rectangle remain; forcing is possible iff fewer than two empty rows or fewer than two empty columns, hence r>=m-1 or d>=n-1. Inclusion-minimal row bases and column bases determine isolated TAR configurations. At budget m, row bases become connected using one temporary added cell; at n−1 the B_{m,n}=n sum_{r=1}^{m−2} binom(m,r)r!Stirling(n−1,r) isolated column bases appear, merging by n. In square case inclusion-exclusion of row and column bases gives 2t^t−t²(t−1)!. Independence checked by direct power-domination forcing on all subsets and explicit TAR BFS for 7 small boards, including the nonmonotone 3×5 profile (75,1,16,1). Universal proof is combinatorial not finite enumeration.
residual_risks: Not a theorem on token jumping, token sliding, other graph products or fixed-cardinality reconfiguration; finite BFS is not all-board proof.

Bjorkman et al. and Curtis et al. give general TAR connectivity/bounds, and a published triangular-graph component spectrum concerns a different graph. None of the inspected mathematical statements determines every two-parameter rook TAR component count with Stirling isolated jump and reentrant connectivity. value.rationale: The full TAR component phase profile of rook power-dominating sets is natural to understanding sensor-set mobility and robustness under a size budget. The reentrant transition from connected to disconnected to connected, with exact Stirling-number multiplicities and unbounded separation of first versus permanent connectivity thresholds, is a structural graph-theoretic phenomenon not implied merely by knowing minimum power-domination numbers.
residual_risks: The exceptional term vanishes at m=2 and empty parameter intervals must be respected; only m>=3 and n>=m+2 has genuine reentrance.

limitations: Result claims no new discovery of known power-domination row/column criterion; novelty is exact TAR component spectrum and sharp reentrance. Finite enumerations corroborate only selected boards.
